Adopts a gender-disaggregated digital-inclusion target inside the country's largest digital programme - approximately 30,000 officials, 40% women, to be trained in regulatory effectiveness, digital governance and service delivery.
Distinct event carrying the only sex-disaggregated digital-skills outcome published in the window: 3 women among 41 machine learning graduates and 18 women graduating in Python.

The published national disability data any inclusion measurement rests on - Washington Group functional-difficulty prevalence disaggregated by sex, age, residence and county. No administrative disability register has been shown to exist, so this is the figure itself. Staged as excerpt after truncation.

Liberia's first CRPD review closes with observations naming barriers in the digital environment including government websites, and gaps in disability data collection - the strongest in-window accountability movement.

Distinct event: the National Commission on Disabilities launches a 2026-2030 plan proposing a Research and Data Management department, a Sign Language and Braille Education department and a monitoring framework.

The enacting instrument for refugee registration and identity: it establishes the LRRRC and the Asylum Committee, entitles every recognized refugee to a prescribed identity card, and empowers the taking of finger-prints, palm-prints and photographs.

The operative step: an LRRRC-NIR-LIS memorandum under Executive Orders 144 and 147 enrolling eligible refugees in the National Biometric Identification System and issuing specialized biometric Refugee Identification cards.

Distinct later event: Executive Order 159 rebrands LRRRC as RAMCO and extends the mandate to IDPs, statelessness and migration governance, with a first National Migration Policy and a national IDP policy framework under way.

The operative universal-access instrument: it creates the Universal Access Fund under sections 22-23 of the Telecommunications Act 2007, with a 0.5% levy on designated licensees and eligibility limited to un-served and under-served areas and disadvantaged groups. Already staged by a sibling slice at this path; my near-duplicate write under a 2015-09-10 prefix was removed.
A completed fund deployment rather than an intention - satellite connectivity installed in Vahun District, Lofa County, recorded by the fund itself.
Distinct event: a commissioned 4G tower bringing first service to Karloken City and Wutuken Township in Maryland County, verified on the ground by the reporter.
The NSDS itself. Signed at Monrovia 15 December 2025 for 2026-2030, superseding NSDS I (2008-2012) and NSDS II (2017-2021); the instrument the indicator asks whether exists.

First national diagnostic of how the statistical system is used and where it fails users, published a month after the strategy was signed. The only in-window movement distinct from the strategy itself.
The census itself: final results of the 2022 National Population and Housing Census, with county and district tables.
First annual agriculture survey after the 2024 agriculture census, dated October 2025 in its own text; the start of a modular post-census survey sequence.
A distinct release: the first national women's empowerment and nutrition module, disseminated alongside the agriculture survey but a separate instrument and report.
The standing compilation of official statistics drawn from ministry and agency administrative records for 2016-2022, and the evidence that Liberia produces statistics from administrative data at all.
The education administrative-data collection moved to school-based digital capture across all 15 counties and 125 districts, run 27 March to 27 April 2026.
A second, separate administrative stream digitised: the emergency patient care report, in use in Montserrado through the National Health Intelligence Center as phase one of a national rollout.

The dated authoritative statement of the open-data position: the EITI Board scorecard as of 23 July 2026, scoring data accessibility and open data 90/100. Sector-specific to extractives, which the note records.

Independent review of the 2024-2026 action plan naming open contracting and beneficial ownership as the promising commitments and finding procurement data online but not machine-readable. Already staged by a sibling slice at this URL; not restaged, selection repointed.
Public-use anonymised microdata released on the LISGIS catalogue, the record carrying its own view and download counts - use rather than availability.

The national earth-observation land-use monitoring system itself: 5,990 plots on a 4km grid read from Sentinel-2, Landsat, MODIS and Planet, with cropland an explicit class and agricultural expansion a named driver.

Farm-level geolocation and digital traceability for cocoa, coffee, rubber and palm oil under the EU deforestation regulation, with a 2020 forest-cover map and 2000-2024 change analysis completed and US$530,000 committed.
A separate event: nationwide soil sampling begun in Bong County to produce national suitability, fertility, land-use and land-cover maps and a first National Digital Soil Information Center.

The standing statement of the observation position: no GBON-compliant surface stations, one operational staffed station, no WIS/GTS transmission, and the PUMA satellite reception workstation underused for power and connectivity.
The baseline's named defect answered: a ClimSA/PUMA2025 Meteosat Third Generation receiving station installed at Roberts International Airport on 24 October 2025.
The Green Climate Fund Liberia CIS project moving to build an automated decision management system for climate services. A procurement notice, not an award, and a short page.

The framework the later instruments sit under: Liberia's own Ministry record of the Belt and Road MoU signed 27 April 2019. The Chinese Embassy English bilateral-relations pages cited by the agent no longer serve that content.
An Agreement on Development Cooperation signed in Monrovia on 9 January 2026, framed by Beijing as implementing the Beijing FOCAC summit outcomes.

Beijing's own record of the 19 May 2026 talks: zero-tariff treatment for Liberian exports and coordination with Liberia on the UN Security Council - positioning rather than assistance, which is what the topic is for.
The only Liberia-specific EU treaty instrument, as published at OJ L 191; signed 27 July 2011, in force 1 December 2013, and the thing the in-window movement acts on.
COM(2025) 467 final: the Commission proposes ending the VPA after a decade without an operative licensing scheme. A proposal, not an adopted termination.

A new EUR 25m grant financing agreement signed at the Ministry of Finance covering all nine coastal counties, linked to Global Gateway. No EU Delegation or ministry primary release was found for the signing.

The standing Gulf bilateral instruments the base can name from a Liberian government source: an air service agreement with Saudi Arabia and a bilateral air services agreement with Qatar, with Emirates talks recorded as preliminary.
US$73.8m of financing agreements signed with the OPEC Fund, BADEA and the Kuwait Fund, plus a separate Saudi Fund commitment of US$49.6m to the Botota-Gbarnga-Zorzor transmission line.
A distinct earlier event: bilateral talks at UNGA 80 with the Crown Prince of Kuwait, financing mobilised for 115km of Bong-Lofa roads and proposed bilateral agreements routed to a Joint Commission.

India's own standing register of the bilateral instruments, last updated 3 September 2026: the four 2013 agreements, the cancelled US$144m Exim credit, the US$50m Exim-supported EBID road credit, ITEC allocations and the 2025 Pharmacopoeia MoU. Substituted for the MEA bilateral brief PDF, which would not resolve.
The newest India-Liberia bilateral instrument in the window, from the Indian mission's own press release: an MoU recognising the Indian Pharmacopoeia in Liberia, signed 11 December 2025.

A separate event: Nyanti-Jaishankar talks in New Delhi on 13 August 2026 with 3,000 tonnes of rice and expanded scholarships committed, alongside the reopening of the resident Liberian embassy in New Delhi.
